specification:
Type: timeline **sim-id:** ephesus-walk-timeline
**Library:** vis-timeline
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** compare
**Learning Objective:** The learner will compare the construction dates of nine monuments passed on the downhill walk through Ephesus, predicting for each one whether it was begun before or after the monument passed just before it, with at least 6 of 8 predictions correct. **Prerequisites:** reading a ruin and spolia (Chapter 4); the Memmius Monument, Curetes Street, the Gate of Hercules, the Fountain of Trajan, the Temple of Hadrian at Ephesus, the terrace houses, the Library of Celsus, the Gate of Mazaeus and Mithridates, the Great Theater of Ephesus, and the Harbor Street (all defined in Parts Three to Six above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The monuments appear one at a time in walking order. For monuments 2 to 9, the learner predicts "older" (begun earlier) or "younger" (begun later) than the previous monument before its date is revealed. A prediction is correct when it matches the Answer column in Content. Mastery is 6 of 8 correct. Dragging or zooming the finished timeline is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A site is built in one period, so neighboring monuments are about the same age (items 2–3, 6–7). (2) The downhill walk runs steadily from older to newer, or the reverse. (3) A monument's construction date is the date of everything in it; the Gate of Hercules is built of older carved blocks (spolia), and the theater was rebuilt over several centuries. **Instructional Rationale:** Comparing each date with the one before forces the learner to hold two monuments in mind and commit to a judgment before seeing the answer, which builds a sense of the city as layers rather than a single snapshot. The finished timeline then shows the zigzag visually. **Content:** Monuments in walking order: | # | Monument (walking order) | Date shown | Bar on the timeline (start to end) | Answer (compared with previous) | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Memmius Monument | Late 1st century BCE | 40 BCE to 1 BCE | (first item, no prediction) | A monument to a grandson of Sulla, from the reign of Augustus. | | 2 | Gate of Hercules | 4th–5th century CE, built with older reliefs | 350 CE to 450 CE | Younger | A late-antique gate built of older carved blocks. | | 3 | Fountain of Trajan | Early 2nd century CE | 102 CE to 114 CE | Older | Built under Trajan, more than two centuries before the gate we just passed. | | 4 | Temple of Hadrian | Dedicated before 138 CE | 117 CE to 138 CE | Younger | Dedicated to Hadrian, Trajan's successor. | | 5 | Terrace House 2 | 1st century BCE to 3rd century CE | 25 BCE to 270 CE | Older | The houses were begun more than a century before the temple and lived in until earthquakes in the 3rd century. | | 6 | Library of Celsus | Begun c. 110 CE | 110 CE to 125 CE | Younger | Begun around 110 CE, long after the first terrace houses. | | 7 | Gate of Mazaeus and Mithridates | 4–3 BCE | 4 BCE to 3 BCE | Older | Built under Augustus, more than a century before the library beside it. | | 8 | Great Theater | First built 3rd century BCE; rebuilt 1st–2nd century CE | Two bars: 290 BCE to 250 BCE, and 41 CE to 117 CE | Older | Its first, Hellenistic building is about three centuries older than the gate; the Roman rebuilding came later. | | 9 | Harbor Street (Arcadiane) | Rebuilt c. 400 CE | 395 CE to 408 CE | Younger | Rebuilt under the emperor Arcadius, who reigned 395–408 CE. | After item 9, a second row shows two reference events: Paul in Ephesus, c. 52–55 CE, and the riot of the silversmiths, c. 55 CE. **Provenance:** Dates from this chapter's sections "Inscription," "Curetes Street," "Hadrian," "The Temple of Hadrian at Ephesus," "The Terrace Houses," "The Library of Celsus," "Greek Theater," and "The Great Theater of Ephesus," and from Chapter 9 for Paul's years. Bar ranges are rounded for display: the sim marks every bar "c." and shows the note "Dates are approximate; most monuments were built over years and repaired for centuries." The Library bar's end, 125 CE, is illustrative, since the completion date is uncertain; the sim labels it so. **Rules:** - Items appear in walking order, 1 to 9. Item 1 has no prediction. - A monument's comparison year is the start of its first bar: 1: −40; 2: 350; 3: 102; 4: 117; 5: −25; 6: 110; 7: −4; 8: −290; 9: 395 (negative numbers are BCE). - For items 2 to 9, "older" is correct when the item's comparison year is less than the previous item's; "younger" when it is greater. No two consecutive items share a comparison year. - One prediction per item; it cannot be changed after the reveal. Score 0 to 8; mastery is score >= 6. - The timeline axis runs from 300 BCE to 500 CE, with no year 0. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees item 1, the Memmius Monument, placed on the timeline. 2. For each later item, the learner reads its name and walking note ("next, on Curetes Street"), predicts older or younger than the previous item, and sees its bar appear with feedback. 3. After item 9, the full timeline shows, with Paul's years marked. 4. The learner drags and zooms the timeline to compare bars. 5. The learner should notice that the walk zigzags across about seven centuries, from about 290 BCE to about 450 CE, and that the riot took place in a theater that was still being rebuilt. **Feedback:** After each prediction: correct shows "Correct. [Why]"; incorrect shows "Not quite: this one is [older/younger]. [Why]". A running count "Correct: n of 8." At the end: "You compared [n] of 8 correctly. Mastery is 6." with a "Walk again" option that restarts from item 1. **Starting State:** An empty timeline from 300 BCE to 500 CE with the first bar, "Memmius Monument, late 1st century BCE," and the question "Walking downhill, is the next monument older or younger?" **Chapter Anchors:** Memmius Monument 1st century BCE; Gate of Hercules probably 4th or 5th century CE, with spolia reliefs; Fountain of Trajan early 2nd century CE; Temple of Hadrian before 138 CE; Hadrian emperor 117–138; terrace houses 1st century BCE to 3rd century CE; Library begun around 110 CE; Gate of Mazaeus and Mithridates 4–3 BCE; theater first built probably in the 3rd century BCE and rebuilt in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE; Harbor Street rebuilt around 400 CE under Arcadius; Paul in Ephesus about 52–55 CE; nine monuments, eight predictions, mastery 6 of 8.
